tokyo_penthouse_ginza_hanare_ginza8.gf_detail: Ask. Steak, beef sashimi and carpaccio with ponzu, rice and miso soup, plus a curry; ponzu and miso usually contain wheat or soy and no source mentions gluten-free handling.
tokyo_penthouse_ginza_hanare_ginza8.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Wagyu sashimi and steak, abalone.
tokyo_penthouse_ginza_hanare_ginza8.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 17:30–22:30 (L.O. 21:30); also listed Sat but noted closed Saturdays; closed Sundays, holidays and irregularly (Tabelog).
tokyo_penthouse_ginza_hanare_ginza8.notes: [Steak · the casual 'hanare' of a members-only steakhouse] The 23-seat annex of PENTHOUSE, a members-only Ginza steakhouse celebrating 50 years. It serves traditional steak casually and holds a licence to serve raw beef. Courses start with very tender beef sashimi and a carpaccio with myōga, red onion and house ponzu. Mains are a choice of two steaks, such as strip loin and filet, or the signature sirloin with a crisp crust, eaten with rice and miso soup. Grilled leeks come with sauce, and a spicy plain curry is also served. Monaka to finish. Quiet on weeknights. One diner found the sides and abalone uneven. Several restaurants share the building, so check the floor. About ¥20,000–30,000.

chef_bio.origin: Sister of PENTHOUSE (50 years, per Tabelog)

anecdotes.text: "The meat carpaccio was incredibly delicious. It was served with slices of myoga (Japanese ginger) and red onion, dressed in a special ponzu sauce." — April 2026.
"The main focus is on beef dishes, starting with sashimi that is incredibly tender, almost like fish… you can choose two types of steak." — October 2026.

tokyo_teppanyaki_colza_ginza7.notes: [Teppanyaki · the soy-sauce maker's own counter] A teppanyaki restaurant run by the Kikkoman group, opened in 1987 and moved to the Toraya Ginza Building in late 2024 as Colza. Interior wood comes from old soy-sauce barrels and the tableware is custom-made. Counter seating plus a private room. The day's ingredients are shown first. Steaks such as sirloin cap or a melt-in-the-mouth strip loin come with a Kikkoman soy sauce made only for Colza, plus onions and fried garlic. The chef's signature course in October 2026 opened with Hokkaidō-soy tofu, autumn truffle and butternut purée, then grilled lobster with persimmon and celery. Suited to business dinners and celebrations.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 1987 by Kikkoman; renewed as Colza in 2024 (2026 review; Tabelog opening 18 November 2024)
chef_bio.philosophy: Traditional technique with new ideas; soy sauce and soybeans to lift umami (Tabelog listing; 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "This is a specialized Teppan-yaki restaurant opened in 1987 by the long-established Kikkoman… The restaurant relocated to the Toraya Ginza Building in Ginza 7-chome two years ago and was renewed as Colza." — October 2026.
"I enjoyed it with a special Kikkoman soy sauce made exclusively for Colza." — October 2026, sirloin cap.

tokyo_vinpicoeur_ginza4.notes: [French bistro · charcoal skewers and fine wine] A counter-centred 24-seat wine bistro off Ginza 4-chōme, part of the group behind auxamis.com. Mains are duck or lamb, and a rice porridge makes a good finish. The sommelier keeps the wine flowing with short, witty notes, and runs monthly by-the-glass fairs (Alsace in October 2026) plus Burgundy specials. About ¥6,000–10,000 a head.

tokyo_ginza_lazy_ginza1.notes: [Italian · a 36-year Ginza 1-chōme favourite] A cosy, lively 25-seat Italian on a seventh floor that is easy to miss, serving creative Italian and wider Mediterranean dishes for 36 years. Per Precious, the menu was shaped by Ichinohe (一戸) with chef Ishikawa (石川) to avoid trend-chasing. Everyone orders the Gorgonzola and French-bread gratin (a small size exists), even people who don't like blue cheese. Also popular: baked oysters, Yoshida Farm caciocavallo baked with tomato, squid-ink risotto, sautéed squid and mushrooms, avocado and vegetable plates, and good pasta. A good wine list. Hard to book at times. ¥500 cover includes garlic toast and water. One diner had heard it might be closing, so check.

chef_bio.background: Menu created by 一戸 (Ichinohe) with chef 石川 at the opening (Precious); ownership not stated.

anecdotes.text: "★★ Gorgonzola Cheese and Bread Gratin (Small Size) ★ Baked Oysters ★ Baked Caciocavallo Cheese from Yoshida Farm with Tomatoes ★ Squid Ink Risotto." — October 2026.
"I heard the restaurant was closing, but I wonder what happened." — September 2026.

tokyo_les_copains_bouchet_ginza5.notes: [French bistro · Dominique Bouchet's bistronomy] A 26-seat basement bistro behind Tokyu Plaza, open since 2016, carrying on the Michelin-starred technique of chef Dominique Bouchet in a warmer bistro style from an open kitchen. Prix-fixe menus let each guest choose fish or meat. October 2026 lunches ran Tosa bonito with mustard, chestnut and truffle soup, sea bream and beef in fine sauces. Earlier French Restaurant Week menus (¥6,000) included shrimp and basil beignets, swordfish, chicken and mushroom pie, and pear tart. French staff and a French sommelier choose and explain wines. Popular for celebrations, and closed through August.

chef_bio.background: Part of the Dominique Bouchet group (2026 review: "part of the Dominique Bouchet chain").
chef_bio.philosophy: Bistronomy — gourmet quality with bistro warmth (Tabelog listing).

tokyo_yakiuo_ishikawa_mitsukoshi.hours_raw: Weekdays 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:00); weekends and holidays 11:00–22:00; closed 1 January (Tabelog).
tokyo_yakiuo_ishikawa_mitsukoshi.notes: [Seafood · fish grilled like yakiniku] A 24-seat restaurant on the 12th floor of the Ginza Mitsukoshi annex (13 at the counter, 9 in a private counter room), opened in 2025. It serves 'yaki-uo', a fish version of yakiniku developed over eight years by the founder of Tsukiji Aozora. Premium cuts are grilled in front of you, such as fatty tuna billed as 'special kalbi', with house condiments and sauces. 2026 diners started with the brain, then had fresh mehikari, a yukhoe-like dish and a sukiyaki-style course (just under ¥4,000 plus ¥400 service). The ladies' lunch adds rice with refills, cold noodles and dessert. The grill staff are chatty. Many guests are visitors from Hong Kong and Singapore. A touch salty, and slow at times.

chef_bio.background: Concept by the founder of Tsukiji Aozora (Tabelog listing, "Ishikawa Tainobu" in the English text); group-run.

anecdotes.text: "The first part we had grilled was the brain, and it felt just like yakiniku! Yet, the essence of the fish was still present." — October 2026.
"The sukiyaki course was just under JPY 4000, with an additional service charge of JPY 400… The clientele was mostly foreign." — October 2026.

tokyo_ginza_fish_burger_nagomi_kyobashi.notes: [Burgers · fish, not beef] A 26-seat fish-burger specialist on a ground floor between Ginza-itchōme and Kyōbashi, open since 2022, with sofa, counter and terrace seats. Rather than battered and fried, the signature mackerel burger (¥1,000) uses a grilled patty of minced fish, with a free dip such as wasabi tartar. Others include a soft-shell crab burger with nuggets (¥1,750), an eel special, shrimp and salmon burgers, mackerel spring rolls and a seafood hot dog. Diners find them light, and the nuggets surprisingly good. Open until midnight.

anecdotes.text: "While chain restaurants usually serve fish burgers that are battered and fried, this place offers a healthier option with a grilled fish patty made from minced fish." — October 2026, ¥1,000 mackerel burger.
"Soft Shell Crab Burger + Chicken Nuggets (JPY 1750)" — July 2026.

tokyo_barchetta_shiodome.notes: [Wine bistro · all-you-can-taste wine in Shiodome] A 24-seat weekday-evening bistro on the second floor of Shiodome City Center, open since 2023. The draw is a free-pour tasting of about 30 wines for ¥1,200 for 60 minutes, extendable by ¥600 per 30 minutes. Dishes run ¥380–1,880. The chicken and vegetable cream stew is the hit; one diner found the ¥1,800 lasagna plain and unlike its menu photo. Course plans with free-flow wine and champagne suit company events, and there's a fully private room for ten. The building's signage is poor, so look for it beside Menya Takeichi.

anecdotes.text: "They offer nearly 30 different wines for an all-you-can-drink price of JPY 1,200 for 60 minutes… The food prices range from JPY 380 to a maximum of JPY 1,880." — February 2026.

tokyo_ginza_tean_soba_kaiseki.notes: [Soba kaiseki · buckwheat in every course] A 26-seat basement restaurant near Takarachō, open since 2019, serving 'sobako kaiseki'. Courses use buckwheat from Aomori's Shirakami mountains and mix Japanese and Western styles. Dishes have included soba dumplings with an oden-like simmered dish, soba folded with egg, simmered clams, soft-shelled turtle, a squid salad, soba served in a wine glass and a signature duck soba with bright-green matcha soba. Courses from ¥6,000. Private rooms for two to eight suit business dinners, and there's a counter and lunch. A freshly renovated 28-seat basement room has a 12-seat counter with five cooks behind it. Expect a short queue at noon and many overseas visitors. Katsudon is the order: the special tenderloin katsudon with an 80 g cutlet and soft egg is admired for its balance, and the black-pork loin katsudon is ¥3,200. tokyo_soba_sasuga_ginza2.notes: [Soba · ultra-thin ju-wari in a Ginza alley] The main shop of Sasuga, a calm, polished soba restaurant up a quiet Ginza 2-chōme alley. It has a 6-seat wooden counter, tables, a private room and a semi-private room. The soba is made by hand from buckwheat alone (ju-wari), cut very thin, with a smooth, springy texture; one 2026 reviewer says it has held a Michelin star. Courses bring soba dumplings, buckwheat with grated yam, tamagoyaki and a sobagaki with sweet red-bean soup to finish. The owner chats about the neighbourhood. It suits a stop after the Kabuki-za.

tokyo_regal_shusse_kaido_ginza8.notes: [Wine bar · charcoal grill on Ginza's 'Shusse-kaidō'] A 28-seat wine bar and kitchen behind a heavy door on the narrow 'Shusse-kaidō' (success road) alley in Ginza 8-chōme. It has a 9-seat counter downstairs and tables and a private room upstairs, where smoking is allowed. The cooking is careful rather than flashy: classic Neapolitan pasta, vongole with big clams, meat grilled over charcoal (served on a crystal plate), butter scallops, bagna cauda, fresh oysters and carpaccio. Some diners found other dishes average, and once the oven was down. Weeknights to 2:30 a.m. 10% service.
